cases.sentence: – Сережа! – сказал славянин-гувернер, остановясь в дверях, ведших во ___. – Сами снимите.
cases.explain: «внутренние комнаты» — after the preposition «во», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Seryozha!” said the tutor, stopping in the doorway leading to the inner rooms. “Take it off yourself.” But Seryozha, though he heard his tutor’s feeble voice, did not pay attention to it. He stood keeping hold of the hall-porter’s belt, and gazing into his face.

cases.explain: «балетная танцовщица» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The porter’s daughter was a ballet dancer.

cases.sentence: – Нет, вы мне только скажите, Василий Лукич, – спросил он вдруг, уже сидя за ___ и держа в руках книгу, – что больше Александра Невского?
cases.explain: «рабочим столом» — after the preposition «за», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “No, do just tell me, Vassily Lukitch,” he asked suddenly, when he was seated at their work table with the book in his hands, “what is greater than the Alexander Nevsky? You know papa’s received the Alexander Nevsky?”

cases.sentence: – Вы бы лучше думали о своей работе, а именины никакого значения не имеют для ___.
cases.explain: «разумного существа» — after the preposition «для», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “You’d much better be thinking about your work. Birthdays are of no importance to a rational being. It’s a day like any other on which one has to do one’s work.”
